title: If I could...
goal: Student uses second conditional to express hypothetical or unlikely situations in present/future, with "were" for all persons (subjunctive) and "I wish + past" for present wishes.
module_chunks: If I had + noun, I would + base
If I were + noun/adj, I would + base
I wish I had / I wish I were
If I were you, I would...
I'd love to / I'd hate to (chunks)

units.title: If I had time
units.grammar_focus: Second conditional structure (If + past simple, would + base)
units.real_life_context: You imagine alternative present realities — what you'd do differently if circumstances were different.

grammar.sentence: If I _____ more time, I would learn piano.
grammar.explanation: Second conditional: "If + past simple, would + base". The "if" clause uses past simple ("had"), even when talking about a hypothetical PRESENT. This is the core structure of the second conditional.

grammar.sentence: If she lived closer, we _____ each other more.
grammar.explanation: The main clause always uses "would + base form". "We would see" — not "we will see" (which would be first conditional, real).

grammar.sentence: If I _____ rich, I would travel the world.
grammar.explanation: In formal/correct second conditional, "were" is used for ALL persons (I, he, she, it, we, you, they). "Were" is the subjunctive form. "Was" is acceptable in informal speech, but "were" is the standard.

grammar.sentence: I _____ help you if I were here.
grammar.explanation: The main clause of the second conditional uses "would + base form". "I would help you" — the if-clause has the past form "were".

grammar.sentence: If I _____ you, I would accept the offer.
grammar.explanation: "If I were you" is the fixed chunk for giving advice. Always "were", never "was" in formal/correct English.

grammar.sentence: She would visit more often if she _____ a car.
grammar.explanation: "If she had a car" — past simple "had" signaling a hypothetical present situation (she doesn't have a car now, but if she did...).

grammar.sentence: If we _____ the lottery, what would we do?
grammar.explanation: "If we won" — past simple "won" in the if-clause signals a hypothetical present. The main clause keeps "would + base form".

grammar.sentence: If I will have time, I would learn piano.
grammar.hint: Após "if", past simple — nunca "will" em second conditional
grammar.answer: If I had time, I would learn piano.
grammar.explanation: Common error: mixing first conditional (will) with second. In second conditional, the "if" clause uses past simple. "If I had" — past simple for a hypothetical present.

grammar.sentence: If I was you, I would say yes.
grammar.answer: If I were you, I would say yes.
grammar.explanation: "Were" is the correct standard for hypothetical advice. "Was" shows up in very informal speech, but "were" is universal.

grammar.passage: If I had more time, I would learn piano. If she lived closer, we would see each other more. If I were rich, I would travel the world.
grammar.question: What would the speaker do if they had more time?
grammar.explanation: The text says "If I had more time, I would learn piano".

If she lived closer, we would see each other more.
If I were rich, I would travel the world.
If I were you, I would accept the offer.
She would visit if she had a car.

units.title: I wish I had
units.grammar_focus: Wishes about present (I wish + past simple)
units.real_life_context: You express dissatisfaction with current reality and longing for something different.

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ more time.
grammar.explanation: "I wish + past simple" for wishes about the present. "I wish I had" — a present wish for more time now (which I don't have).

grammar.sentence: She wishes she _____ taller.
grammar.explanation: "Were" for all persons in formal wish/hypothetical. "She wishes she were taller" — present wish about height.

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ speak French.
grammar.explanation: "I wish I could + base" for ability wishes. "Could" is the "past" of "can" in hypothetical wishes.

grammar.sentence: He wishes he _____ a better job.
grammar.explanation: Wish + past simple for a present situation. "He had" — past simple of the verb "have".

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ younger.
grammar.explanation: "I wish I were younger" — present wish about age. "Were" is the correct standard.

grammar.sentence: We wish we _____ in a bigger house.
grammar.explanation: "We wish we lived in a bigger house" — present wish about housing.

grammar.sentence: I wish I _____ play the guitar.
grammar.explanation: "I wish I could play" — ability wish. "Could" is the "past" used in wish.

grammar.sentence: I wish I have more time.
grammar.hint: Wish para presente usa past simple
grammar.answer: I wish I had more time.
grammar.explanation: "Wish" about the present uses past simple. "I wish I have" doesn't work — always past simple in wish.

grammar.sentence: I wish I would be taller.
grammar.hint: Para wish sobre presente, past simple "were"
grammar.explanation: "Would" doesn't combine with wish about the present. For current wishes about characteristics, use past simple "were".

grammar.passage: I wish I had more free time. She wishes she were taller. We wish we could speak more languages. He wishes he lived closer to family.
grammar.question: What does she wish she were?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She wishes she were taller".

units.title: If I were you
units.grammar_focus: Advice with "If I were you, I would..." (subjunctive in advice)
units.real_life_context: You give advice diplomatically by imagining yourself in someone else's position.

grammar.sentence: If I _____ you, I would talk to her.
grammar.explanation: "If I were you" is the fixed chunk for formal advice. Always "were", even with "I". This is the subjunctive form preserved in modern English.

grammar.sentence: If I were you, I _____ accept the offer.
grammar.explanation: "I would accept" — would + base in the main clause. Standard second-conditional advice pattern.

grammar.sentence: If I _____ you, I would say sorry.
grammar.explanation: "Were" is universal for advice — more polite and grammatically correct than "was".

grammar.sentence: _____ I were you, I'd take the job.
grammar.explanation: "If I were you" — starts with "if". "When/although" don't work in this chunk.

grammar.sentence: If I were you, I _____ go for it.
grammar.explanation: "Would go for it" — natural encouragement chunk in the main clause.

grammar.sentence: If I _____ in your position, I would think twice.
grammar.explanation: "If I were in your position" — variation of the core chunk. Keeps "were".

grammar.sentence: I _____ talk to him if I were you.
grammar.explanation: "I would talk" — "would" in the main clause, even with reversed sentence order.

grammar.sentence: If I was you, I would say yes.
grammar.answer: If I were you, I would say yes.
grammar.explanation: "If I was" is very informal speech and considered incorrect in formal writing. "Were" is the universal standard.

grammar.sentence: If I were you, I will accept it.
grammar.answer: If I were you, I would accept it.
grammar.explanation: Second conditional always uses "would + base" in the main clause, never "will" (that's first conditional).

grammar.passage: If I were you, I would talk to her honestly. If I were in your position, I would take the offer. If I were you, I would go for it — life is short.
grammar.question: What does the speaker think you should do?
grammar.explanation: The text suggests multiple actions; all are valid advice given in the second conditional with "if I were you".

units.title: What would you do?
units.grammar_focus: Questions in second conditional (Would you + base + if?)
units.real_life_context: You ask hypothetical questions to explore values and choices.

grammar.sentence: What _____ you do if you won the lottery?
grammar.explanation: Second conditional question: "WH + would + subject + base + if + past simple". "What would you do?" — standard hypothetical question.

grammar.sentence: _____ you travel if you had more money?
grammar.explanation: Yes/no question in second conditional: "Would + subject + base + if + past simple?".

grammar.sentence: Where _____ you live if you could choose any country?
grammar.explanation: "Would you live" — WH + would + subject + base.

grammar.sentence: If you _____ a million dollars, what would you do?
grammar.explanation: After "if" in second conditional, always past simple. "Had a million" — hypothetical situation.

grammar.sentence: What would you do if you _____ in my position?
grammar.explanation: "If you were in my position" — hypothetical scenario uses "were" (subjunctive) in the if-clause.

grammar.sentence: Would you change jobs if you _____ the chance?
grammar.explanation: "If you had the chance" — past simple in the if-clause of a hypothetical question.

grammar.sentence: Where would you go if you _____ a free week?
grammar.explanation: "If you had a free week" — past simple "had" signals a hypothetical present in the if-clause.

grammar.sentence: What will you do if you won the lottery?
grammar.answer: What would you do if you won the lottery?
grammar.explanation: Winning the lottery is hypothetical (unlikely), so second conditional with "would". "Will" would be first conditional (more likely).

grammar.sentence: Would you to help me if I asked?
grammar.answer: Would you help me if I asked?
grammar.explanation: After "would", base form without "to". "Would you help" — natural question.

grammar.passage: What would you do if you won the lottery? Where would you live if you could choose any country? Would you travel more if you had more money?
grammar.question: What hypothetical involves winning the lottery?
accepts: what to do with the money
